entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 44 Jr 44:1-30 . Jeremiah Reproves the Jews for Their Idolatry in Egypt, and Denounces God's Judgments on Them and Egypt Alike. 1. Migdol-- meaning a "tower." A city east of Egypt, towards the Red Sea ( Ex 14:2 ; Nu 33:7 ). Noph-- Memphis, now Cairo ( Jr 2:16 ). Pathros-- Upper Egypt ( Is 11:11 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10534"/><div sID="gen18783" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10534"/><hi type="bold">14. none ... shall escape ... that they should return, &c.--</hi>The Jews had gone to Egypt with the idea that a return to Judea, which they thought hopeless to their brethren in Babylon, would be an easy matter to themselves in Egypt: the exact reverse should happen in the case of each respectively. The Jews whom God sent to Babylon were there weaned from idolatry, and were restored; those who went to Egypt by their perverse will were hardened in idolatry, and perished there.<div eID="gen18783" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18784" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">have a desire--</hi>literally, "lift up (their) soul," that is, their hopes (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.22.27">Jr 22:27</reference>, Margin; <reference osisRef="Deut.24.15">De 24:15</reference>, Margin).<div eID="gen18784" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18785" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">none shall return but such as shall escape--</hi>namely, the "small number" (<reference osisRef="Jer.44.28">Jr 44:28</reference>) who were brought by force into Egypt, as Jeremiah and Baruch, and those who, in accordance with Jeremiah's advice, should flee from Egypt before the arrival of the Chaldeans (see on <reference osisRef="Jer.42.17">Jr 42:17</reference>). Calvin less probably refers the words to the return of the exiles in Babylon, which the Jews in Egypt regarded as hopeless. <div eID="gen18785" type="x-p"/>

So Esau ( He 12:16 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10539"/><div sID="gen18794" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10539"/><hi type="bold">19. make ... cakes to worship her--</hi>Maurer translates, "to form her image." Crescent-shaped cakes were offered to the moon. Vulgate supports English Version.<div eID="gen18794" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18795" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">without our men--</hi>The women mentioned (<reference osisRef="Jer.44.15">Jr 44:15</reference>); "a great multitude" here speak: we have not engaged in secret night orgies which might justly be regarded unfavorably by our husbands: our sacred rites have been open, and with their privity. They wish to show how unreasonable it is that Jeremiah should oppose himself alone to the act of all, not merely women, but men also. The guilty, like these women, desire to shield themselves under the complicity of others. Instead of helping one another towards heaven, husband and wife often ripen one another for hell. <div eID="gen18795" type="x-p"/>

I have sworn--</hi>I, too have made a vow which I will fulfil. Since ye will not hear Me speaking and warning, hear Me swearing.<div eID="gen18802" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18803" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">by my great name--</hi>that is, by Myself (<reference osisRef="Gen.22.16">Ge 22:16</reference>), the greatest by whom God can swear (<reference osisRef="Heb.6.13">He 6:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Heb.6.14">14</reference>).<div eID="gen18803" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18804" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">my name shall no more be named--</hi>The Jews, heretofore, amidst all their idolatry, had retained the form of appeal to the name of God and the law, the distinctive glory of their nation; God will allow this no more (<reference osisRef="Ezek.20.39">Eze 20:39</reference>): there shall be none left there to profane His name thus any more. <div eID="gen18804" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 26. I have sworn-- I, too have made a vow which I will fulfil. Since ye will not hear Me speaking and warning, hear Me swearing. by my great name-- that is, by Myself ( Ge 22:16 ), the greatest by whom God can swear ( He 6:13 , 14 ). my name shall no more be named-- The Jews, heretofore, amidst all their idolatry, had retained the form of appeal to the name of God and the law, the distinctive glory of their nation; God will allow this no more ( Eze 20:39 ): there shall be none left there to profane His name thus any more.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10546"/><div sID="gen18810" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10546"/><hi type="bold">29. this ... sign unto you--</hi>The calamity of Pharaoh-hophra (see on <reference osisRef="Jer.44.30">Jr 44:30</reference>) shall be a sign to you that as he shall fall before his enemy, so you shall subsequently fall before Nebuchadnezzar (<reference osisRef="Matt.24.8">Mt 24:8</reference>) [Grotius]. Calvin makes the "sign" to be simultaneous with the event signified, not antecedent to it, as in <reference osisRef="Exod.3.12">Ex 3:12</reference>. The Jews believed Egypt impregnable, so shut in was it by natural barriers. The Jews being "punished in this place" will be a sign that their view is false, and God's threat true. He calls it "a sign unto you," because God's prediction is equivalent to the event, so that they may even now take it as a sign. When fulfilled it would cease to be a sign to them: for they would be dead. <div eID="gen18810" type="x-p"/>
